drills.title: Cart total with an accumulator
drills.prompt: Arrange and indent the lines so the program adds up the three prices in the cart and then prints the average. Two lines do not belong.
drills.explain: The accumulator pattern has three parts: a start value before the loop (total = 0), an update inside the loop (total += price, indented), and the use of the result after the loop (not indented, so it runs once). total = price would throw away the earlier prices on every round, and the for line needs its colon.

drills.title: Range: stop, step, countdown
drills.prompt: Fill the three blanks so the program prints the goal output. The stop of a range is never included.
drills.explain: range(1, 4) starts at 1 and stops before 4, so it gives 1, 2, 3. To count down you need a negative step: range(3, 0, -1) gives 3, 2, 1 (a step of 1 would give nothing, because 3 is already past 0 going up). The third number of range is the step: range(0, 10, 2) gives 0, 2, 4, 6, 8.

drills.title: continue, break and the loop variable
drills.prompt: Read the code and type exactly what it prints, one line per line of output.
drills.explain: continue skips the rest of that round (3 is not added). break leaves the loop at once (6 is not added), so total is 1 + 2 + 4 + 5 and the loop variable n keeps the value 6 after the loop. A while loop stops when its condition turns False, so count ends at exactly 3. range(2, 10, 3) gives 2, 5, 8 and end=" " keeps them on one line.

drills.title: The table that stops at 9
drills.prompt: The multiplication table of 7 should run from 7 x 1 to 7 x 10, but the last line is missing. Click the faulty line and choose the fix.
drills.explain: range excludes its stop value, so range(1, 10) ends at 9. To include 10 the stop must be 11. range(10) and range(0, 10) start at 0 and also stop at 9, and 12 would print an extra row. Off-by-one errors never crash: check the first and last line of the output.

drills.title: Review the AI's PIN checker
drills.prompt: The ATM rule: the customer gets at most 3 attempts, and after 3 wrong PINs the card must be blocked with a message. An AI assistant wrote this checker. It runs, but it does not follow the rule. Tick the real problems.

issues.text: The loop never stops after 3 wrong attempts, so the 4th guess still unlocks the account
issues.why: The for loop runs over every guess and nothing checks attempts. Stop when attempts reaches 3 (for example break after the third wrong guess, or loop over the first three guesses only).

issues.text: When no guess is right, the program ends without ever blocking the card or saying so
issues.why: Nothing runs after the loop to report the failure. A for ... else (the else runs only when there was no break) or an if attempts == 3 check after the loop would print the "Card blocked" message.

non_issues.text: A for loop is the wrong tool here and it must be a while loop
non_issues.why: Looping over a fixed set of guesses is a normal use of for. The bugs are the missing limit and the missing message, not the kind of loop.

non_issues.text: break on line 7 should be continue
non_issues.why: After a correct PIN there is nothing left to check, so leaving the loop with break is right. continue would keep reading guesses.

non_issues.text: The PIN is stored as text, so it should be an int
non_issues.why: A PIN is an identifier, not a quantity. Text keeps leading zeros ("0492"), and comparing text with text is correct.

non_issues.text: attempts += 1 is after the if, so the counter is off by one
non_issues.why: The line only runs for wrong guesses, which is what "attempts used" counts. A correct guess leaves the loop first.

drills.explain: A loop must stop for the reasons in the rules. Check three things in loop code: when does it end, what happens when it ends WITHOUT finding what it was looking for, and does the counter count the right thing?
